title: Company-wide policies and process documentation
author: Rebecca Moore
content:
Overview:

This consolidated reference describes Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. The document is intended for use by employees, managers, and cross-functional partners who implement or enforce these policies.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors with access to company systems or data.
- Covers corporate systems (G Suite, Okta, internal tools), production services, vendor relationships, procurement workflows, travel & expense reimbursement, and standardized templates for common processes.

Ownership and Contacts:
- Policy owner: People Ops (owner_team)
- Primary contacts: Rebecca Moore (People Ops), Security liaison: Daniel Rivera, Finance lead: Aisha Patel
- Questions and exception requests: policies@redwoodinference.com

1) Access & Permissions
Purpose: Ensure least-privilege access, clear ownership, and a predictable approval and audit trail for access changes.

Policy summary:
- All user access to corporate systems must be provisioned through Okta SSO and matched to role-based groups.
- Production access (read/write to runtime clusters, GPU pools, or customer data stores) requires two approvals: an application owner and a security reviewer.
- Temporary elevated access (break-glass) is granted via the approved emergency access workflow and is time-limited (default 8 hours).

Provisioning procedure (numbered):
1. Requester opens an access request in the IT service portal and selects the target application and role.
2. Request routes to the resource owner for approval (owner must be named in the service onboarding record).
3. Security reviews requests that include production or PII access.
4. Upon approval, OKTA group membership is updated automatically by the provisioning service.
5. The ticket is closed with justification, and the change is recorded for quarterly audits.

Roles & responsibilities (bullets):
- Resource Owner: maintains an up-to-date access roster and approves join/leave requests.
- People Ops: periodic user lifecycle management, termination processing.
- Security: approves production/PII access and reviews break-glass requests.
- IT / SRE: implements provisioning and runs monthly orphaned-account checks.

Segregation of Duties table (text table format):
"Role | Approve Access | Deploy to Prod | Modify Billing"
"Service Owner | X |  | "
"Security |  | X (review) | "
"Finance |  |  | X"

Access review cadence:
- Quarterly automated access reports generated by the IAM system; owners must certify within 7 business days.
- Ad-hoc reviews for high-risk services monthly.

Emergency access (break-glass):
- Process: PagerDuty incident -> on-call approves -> create time-limited role in AWS/GCP -> Security performs post-facto review within 48 hours.

2) Change Management
Objective: Minimize risk and ensure predictable, auditable changes to production and critical infrastructure.

Change categories:
- Standard changes: low-risk, pre-approved (routine cert renewal, small config updates).
- Normal changes: require RFC, staging validation, and scheduled maintenance window.
- Emergency changes: unplanned, documented after the fact with rollback plan.

Change process (high-level):
1. Raise RFC in the Change Management system with: scope, owner, rollback plan, test plan, and risk assessment.
2. Peer review and application-owner sign-off.
3. Change Advisory Board (CAB) reviews medium/high risk changes weekly.
4. Schedule change into maintenance window; notify stakeholders 72/48/24 hours depending on customer impact.
5. Execute change; run post-change validation and update runbooks if behavior changed.

Approval matrix (plain bullets):
- Low-risk: service owner sign-off only.
- Medium-risk: service owner + security + SRE.
- High-risk: CAB approval (includes Finance for changes with cost impact > $25k).

Emergency change handling:
- Must include a rollback plan and post-mortem within 5 business days.
- Any emergency production code change requires a follow-up security review for potential regression or exposure.

3) Data Management
Principles: classify, minimize, protect, and retain only as required.

Data classification levels (definitions):
- Public: non-sensitive marketing and product collateral.
- Internal: operational data not containing PII.
- Confidential: internal business information with limited distribution.
- Restricted: PII, customer data, model training data where contractual/regulatory restrictions apply.

Storage & handling rules:
- Restricted data must be stored in approved vaults (encrypted at rest with KMS) and accessed only via logged service accounts.
- Backups: daily incremental, weekly full; retention as per retention schedule below.
- Transmission: TLS 1.2+ for all network transfers; keys must be rotated per KMS policy.

Retention schedule (table-style lines):
"Data Type | Retention Period | Owner"
"Logs (non-PII) | 90 days | Eng-SRE"
"Customer restricted data | per contract (default 7 years) | Sales/Legal"
"Payroll | 7 years | Finance"

Data deletion & de-identification:
- Deletion requests follow the Data Subject Request (DSR) process owned by Security/Privacy.
- Pseudonymization required for datasets used in research; direct identifiers removed and a mapping key stored in KMS-protected vault.

4) Procurement & Expenses
Aim: Ensure proper approvals, vendor diligence, and predictable financial commitments.

Procurement workflow (steps):
1. Requester submits Purchase Request (PR) including justification, budget code, and vendor details.
2. Manager approval required for any PR > $1,000.
3. Finance reviews and routes to procurement for RFPs or vendor onboarding if > $25,000 annual commitment.
4. Legal reviews vendor agreements for standard terms and data protections.
5. PO issued by Procurement; vendor onboarding checklist completed prior to first invoice.

Expense & travel policy highlights:
- Reimbursement requires original receipts; per-diem limits apply for international travel.
- Pre-approval required for travel > $2,000 or longer than 5 business days.
- Company card usage: cardholders must upload receipts within 5 business days; reconciliations monthly.

Approval matrix (bulleted):
- < $1,000: Manager sign-off
- $1,000-$25,000: Manager + Finance
- > $25,000 annual: Procurement + Legal + Finance

Vendor onboarding checklist (short list):
- Completed vendor profile and W-9 / equivalent
- Security questionnaire if the vendor will access systems or data (SOC2 / ISO27001 preferred)
- Signed contract with data processing addendum where necessary
- Payment terms established and PO issued

5) Vendor Management
Goal: Maintain vendor performance, security posture, and clear renewal/termination terms.

Vendor lifecycle (phases):
- Selection: RFP, security assessment, reference checks.
- Onboarding: contract + security posture + payment setup.
- Monitoring: quarterly performance reviews, SLA compliance, and security re-assessments annually.
- Offboarding: terminate access, collect assets, and archive contract.

Escalation & termination triggers (examples):
- Repeated SLA breaches (2+ incidents in 90 days) -> formal remediation plan and escalation to Procurement Director.
- Security incident attributable to vendor -> immediate suspension of access pending review.

6) Travel Policies
Principles: safety, cost-effectiveness, and compliance.

Booking & approvals:
- Book travel through the corporate travel portal; manager pre-approval required for all in-person conferences and customer visits.
- Economy class for flights < 6 hours, premium economy or business for flights > 6 hours with manager approval.

Reimbursement rules:
- Itemized receipts required.
- Per-diem caps: domestic $75/day, international varies by country (refer to travel portal).
- Alcohol allowed on business meals but must be reasonable and within per-diem or expense limits.

Safety & incidents:
- Register travel plans with People Ops; emergency contact available 24/7.
- Report any travel incident to People Ops within 24 hours.

7) Internal Templates and Forms
Included templates (canonical location: /confluence/templates):
- Access request form (link: /confluence/templates/access-request)
- Change Request (RFC) template (link: /confluence/templates/rfc)
- Vendor onboarding checklist (link: /confluence/templates/vendor-onboarding)
- Travel & expense form (link: /confluence/templates/travel-expense)

Sample RFC template (inline snippet):

Enforcement and exceptions:
- Violations of these policies may result in disciplinary action up to termination.
- Exceptions must be requested via the Exception Request form and approved by People Ops + Security (for technical/data exceptions) and documented for audit.
